title: Day 1: Options Trading Bot. Up 25%
author: Lumpy-Owl-7795
selftext:
Built an AI SPY 0DTE Live trading bot. Super easy to set up, the bot checks my TradingView account every 1mins and place an OCO order for my Webull. 

  
The bot also updates its memory to adjust if it makes any profit or loss (so basically it fixes itself).

  
I'm starting with $450. up 25% today. Budget per trade is $400.

  
I trade options only

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: day one on $450 with $400 a trade is one coin flip, and 0DTE SPY is the coin that moves fastest. what I'd push back on is the memory that rewrites itself after each win or loss: that is fitting to the last trade, so the bot you have on Friday is a different bot from the one that was up today. give the Friday version a few weeks on paper before it touches the Webull account. I run that trial on Quantradin, which I built for exactly this: same rule, paper book, live prices, options filled at the bid or the ask. quantradin.com

replies.author: Lumpy-Owl-7795
replies.body:
Ha I see. You mean generating divergent skills to sew which one has the best pnl? So the agent does have the chance to not edit anything tho. Only touches the files that changes. 

Also I have a user feedback system that stay permanent

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: not quite, I meant the opposite. if each loss rewrites a file, a week from now you can't tell which version made which trade. freeze one version, log its trades, and only change it once there are enough trades to judge. keeping the feedback system fixed helps with that.

replies.author: Technical-Athlete-9
replies.body: This is sound advice. And you don’t have to lose your next $400 on that.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: right, and a week of paper first costs nothing. I built Quantradin for that stage, quantradin.com, a bot runs on live prices with fake money and you see the bad days before they're real ones.

replies.author: Lumpy-Owl-7795
replies.body: Quantradin.com sounds really cool. Does it do options?

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: yep, US options. buys fill at the ask and sells at the bid, so a 0DTE bot pays the spread on every round trip, same as it would on Webull.
